summary: Innovation: DNA (Dual-stream Nexus Attention) lets behavior tokens update themselves at each layer by attending to the request representation that just read them, rather than repeatedly projecting a fixed sequence into keys and values. Why it matters: Evolving sequence representations unlock depth scaling, improving CTR estimation and ranking for users with long behavior histories.
title: DNA: Unlocking Depth Scaling in CTR Models

summary: Innovation: X-split Argus trains a history compressor and online ranker end-to-end to encode long histories into reusable offline tokens, distilled from a teacher that sees the uncompressed history, for online cross-attention scoring. Why it matters: Reusable compressed history tokens cut per-candidate ranking cost while preserving CTR-relevant preferences, enabling richer user modeling in latency-constrained ad ranking.
title: X-split Argus: Learning Reusable History Tokens for Efficient CTR Prediction

summary: Innovation: TokenFormer V2 decouples representation resolution from interaction density via group-wise tokens, hierarchical group merging, and NS Fusion and Global Sync modules for local-global modeling. Why it matters: Preserving fine-grained behavior evidence at lower interaction cost can improve ranking quality for long histories within strict serving budgets.
title: TokenFormer V2: Breaking the Resolution-Complexity Dilemma in Unified Recommendation

summary: Innovation: It distills logged serving pCTR scores into ESMM's auxiliary CTR tower, weighted by KD-α, to align training-time and serving-time pCTCVR. Why it matters: Serving-aligned pCTCVR improves CTR/CVR estimation at serving time, so ranking decisions better reflect expected post-click conversion value.
title: Serving-Aligned Entire-Space Conversion Modeling via Click-Through Rate Knowledge Distillation

summary: Innovation: It formulates Context Hint Optimization and introduces CHO-Bench, with seven What, Who, and When hint-generation strategies plus a unified strategy, evaluated in over 1.19 million paired ad-ranking comparisons. Why it matters: Better context hints help LLM ad systems target conversational intent beyond explicit search, improving which ads rank for a given user conversation under a budget.
title: CHO-Bench: How Do Context Hints Affect Ad Rankings in LLM Advertising?

summary: Innovation: It augments recent behavior with separate query-nearest-neighbor and candidate-nearest-neighbor retrieval over long-term history, plus candidate-aware early fusion into every history token and dedicated query and candidate context tokens. Why it matters: Query- and candidate-specific history retrieval improves sponsored-product ranking relevance, raising CTR and conversions by matching long-term behavior to immediate search intent.
title: Query- and Candidate-Aware Long User Sequence Modeling for Sponsored Product Ranking in Search

summary: Innovation: SlimFM compresses LLaMA3-8B by 44% with dependency-aware structured pruning, adapts it with field-aware LoRA to produce field-level semantic embeddings, and fuses those embeddings into a CTR model for online serving. Why it matters: Online LLM semantic embeddings can improve CTR estimation, especially for cold-start and long-tail items, without prohibitive ranking latency.
title: Slim Foundation Models for Latency-Critical Recommendation Serving

summary: Innovation: It shows LLM persona simulation for cold-start ads works best with a minimal demographic anchor without noisy rich attributes, a relative qualitative banner-blindness signal instead of quantitative CTR anchors, and carefully chosen prompt phrasing. Why it matters: Better cold-start persona simulation improves pre-launch targeting and performance estimation, helping advertisers allocate spend across demographic segments without historical logs.
title: What Matters for LLM Persona Simulation: Signal Form in Cold-Start E-Commerce Advertising

summary: Innovation: It uses diverse non-conversion user events and metadata as auxiliary supervision for CVR, with linearized labels, a split training architecture, and Label Combination (LaCo) to handle noisy auxiliary signals. Why it matters: Richer auxiliary signals alleviate sparse conversions, improving CVR estimation in ads ranking so impressions are delivered to users likelier to convert.
title: Improving Ads Ranking Models with Auxiliary Supervision: Techniques and Insights

summary: Innovation: GR4AD-X upgrades generative ad recommendation with more reliable semantic ID construction, serving-efficient capacity scaling, and finer-grained value optimization for intermediate SID decisions. Why it matters: It improves ad retrieval and ranking by keeping potentially high-value candidates from being prematurely pruned while staying within real-time serving limits.
title: Towards Reliable, Scalable, and Value-Aligned Generative Recommendation for Large-Scale Advertising
